settings.title: Anthropic API version
settings.summary: The version the Anthropic adapter says it speaks.
settings.description: The value the Anthropic adapter sends in the anthropic-version header. Gateways that speak the Messages API, such as Ollama and LiteLLM, expect this one.

settings.title: Anthropic retries
settings.summary: How many times a failed Anthropic call is sent again.
settings.description: How many times the Anthropic adapter sends a call again when it failed before any of the reply arrived and the failure may pass: a rate limit, a busy provider, or an endpoint that could not be reached. Zero means never.

settings.title: Anthropic first retry wait
settings.summary: How long the Anthropic adapter waits before its first retry.
settings.description: How long the Anthropic adapter waits before its first retry. Each later wait is twice the one before.

settings.title: Anthropic longest retry wait
settings.summary: The longest the Anthropic adapter waits before a retry.
settings.description: The longest the Anthropic adapter waits before a retry. When the provider asks for a longer wait, the call fails at once so another model can be tried.

settings.title: Anthropic start time limit
settings.summary: How long an Anthropic endpoint may take to begin its answer.
settings.description: How long an endpoint that speaks the Anthropic Messages API may take to begin its answer. A local model that has to be loaded first needs the time. Zero means no limit.

settings.title: Anthropic quiet time limit
settings.summary: How long an Anthropic reply may go quiet before it is given up.
settings.description: How long a reply from the Anthropic adapter's endpoint may send nothing before the call is given up. Zero means no limit.

settings.title: Anthropic prompt caching
settings.summary: Marks calls so the provider can cache what repeats.
settings.description: Whether the Anthropic adapter marks the end of the system blocks and of the last message so the provider can cache what comes before.

settings.title: Models with a thinking budget
settings.summary: The models asked to think within a fixed budget.
settings.description: The provider model names, separated by commas, that are asked for thinking as a token budget. A name ending in * matches by its start. Every other model is asked for adaptive thinking, where the model decides how much to think.

settings.title: Models that take an effort
settings.summary: The models sent a request's effort as the API's own effort setting.
settings.description: The provider model names, separated by commas, that are sent a request's effort as output_config.effort. A name ending in * matches by its start. Another model with the thinking capability is asked to think within the budget the effort stands for instead, and a model with neither is sent nothing about effort.

settings.title: Thinking budget for low effort
settings.summary: The thinking budget low effort stands for in the Anthropic adapter.
settings.description: The thinking tokens a request at low effort may use, for a model with the thinking capability. A model that takes a thinking budget is sent it, kept under the output limit; under 1024 no thinking is asked for. Another model is asked for adaptive thinking.

settings.title: Thinking budget for medium effort
settings.summary: The thinking budget medium effort stands for in the Anthropic adapter.
settings.description: The thinking tokens a request at medium effort may use, for a model with the thinking capability. A model that takes a thinking budget is sent it, kept under the output limit.

settings.title: Thinking budget for high effort
settings.summary: The thinking budget high and higher effort stand for in the Anthropic adapter.
settings.description: The thinking tokens a request at high effort may use, for a model with the thinking capability. Requests at xhigh and max effort use it too. A model that takes a thinking budget is sent it, kept under the output limit.

settings.title: Fake reply piece size
settings.summary: How many characters the fake model sends at a time.
settings.description: How many characters the fake provider sends in each piece of a streamed reply. Zero sends each block in one piece.

settings.title: Fake reply pace
settings.summary: How long the fake model waits between pieces of a reply.
settings.description: How long the fake provider waits before each piece of a streamed reply, so a chat in the test tenant streams at a speed a person can watch. Tests use no wait.

settings.title: Fake vector size
settings.summary: How many numbers each vector from the fake model holds.
settings.description: How many numbers each vector the fake provider makes holds, when a registry entry on the fake adapter is an embedding model, from 1 to 65536. Zero makes the fake make no vectors.

settings.title: Models for each person
settings.summary: The most models one person may set up.
settings.description: The most models one person's registry may hold. Adding one more is refused.

settings.title: Characters for each token
settings.summary: How many characters count as one token in an estimate.
settings.description: How many characters of text count as one token when Keystone estimates a call's size because the provider offers no count. Lower counts more tokens, which is the safe side.

settings.title: Estimate margin
settings.summary: The safety margin added to an estimated size.
settings.description: The safety margin added to an estimated token count, as a percentage of it. A provider's own count gets no margin.

settings.title: Tokens for each message
settings.summary: Extra tokens counted for every message in an estimate.
settings.description: Tokens counted for each message in an estimate, for its role and framing, on top of its content.

settings.title: Tokens for each tool
settings.summary: Extra tokens counted for every tool in an estimate.
settings.description: Tokens counted for each tool offered in an estimate, on top of its name, description and schema.

settings.title: Tokens for each image
settings.summary: Tokens counted for every image in an estimate.
settings.description: Tokens counted for each image in an estimate, whatever its size.

settings.title: Tokens for each named file
settings.summary: Tokens counted for a file whose size cannot be seen.
settings.description: Tokens counted in an estimate for a file that is named by reference, whose size the estimate cannot see.

settings.title: Responses retries
settings.summary: How many times a failed Responses call is sent again.
settings.description: How many times the Responses adapter sends a call again when it failed before any of the reply arrived and the failure is one that may pass. Zero sends each call once.

settings.title: Responses first retry wait
settings.summary: How long the Responses adapter waits before its first retry.
settings.description: How long the Responses adapter waits before its first retry. The wait doubles with each retry.

settings.title: Responses longest retry wait
settings.summary: The longest the Responses adapter waits before a retry.
settings.description: The longest the Responses adapter waits before a retry. When the provider asks for a longer wait, the call fails at once so another model can be tried.

settings.title: Responses start time limit
settings.summary: How long the Responses adapter waits for a reply to begin.
settings.description: How long the Responses adapter waits for a reply to begin before it gives up on the call.

settings.title: Responses quiet time limit
settings.summary: How long a Responses reply may go quiet before it is given up.
settings.description: How long a streamed reply through the Responses adapter may send nothing before it is given up on.

settings.title: Medium effort from
settings.summary: The thinking budget at which medium effort is asked for.
settings.description: The thinking budget, in tokens, from which the Responses adapter asks for medium reasoning effort. A smaller budget asks for low.

settings.title: High effort from
settings.summary: The thinking budget at which high effort is asked for.
settings.description: The thinking budget, in tokens, from which the Responses adapter asks for high reasoning effort.

settings.title: Chat Completions connect time limit
settings.summary: How long the Chat Completions adapter waits to connect.
settings.description: How long the Chat Completions adapter waits to connect to an endpoint, and again to finish the TLS handshake.

settings.title: Chat Completions start time limit
settings.summary: How long a Chat Completions endpoint may take to begin its answer.
settings.description: How long the Chat Completions adapter waits for an endpoint to start its answer. A local model that is still loading needs the time.

settings.title: Chat Completions quiet time limit
settings.summary: How long a Chat Completions reply may go quiet before it ends.
settings.description: How long the Chat Completions adapter waits between two pieces of a streamed reply before it ends the call.

settings.title: Chat Completions attempts
settings.summary: How many times one Chat Completions call is sent at most.
settings.description: How many times the Chat Completions adapter sends one call at most, when the endpoint is busy or cannot be reached. One means no retry.

settings.title: Chat Completions first retry wait
settings.summary: How long the Chat Completions adapter waits before it retries.
settings.description: How long the Chat Completions adapter waits before it sends a call again. The wait doubles with each attempt.

settings.title: Chat Completions sends effort
settings.summary: Sends a request's effort to Chat Completions models that can think.
settings.description: Whether the Chat Completions adapter sends a request's effort as reasoning_effort, for an entry with the thinking capability. Off, nothing about effort is sent, because an endpoint that does not know the field may refuse the call.

settings.title: Summary model
settings.summary: The model that writes summaries of your chats.
settings.description: The registry name of the model that writes summaries of a chat. Empty, or a name that is not in the registry, uses the chat's own model.

settings.title: Memory model
settings.summary: The model that picks out facts to remember.
settings.description: The registry name of the model that runs the memory pass after a turn. Empty, or a name that is not in the registry, uses the chat's own model.

settings.title: Embedding model
settings.summary: The model that turns text into vectors for meaning search.
settings.description: The registry name of the model that turns text into vectors. It must have the embedding capability.

settings.title: Fallback models
settings.summary: The models to try, in order, when a call fails.
settings.description: Registry names, separated by commas, of the models to try in order when the model a call was meant for fails before any of its reply arrived. Empty means a failed call is not sent to another model.

settings.title: Fallbacks for one call
settings.summary: The most other models one failed call is sent to.
settings.description: The most other models one call is sent to after the first one failed. Zero means none.

settings.title: Decision call timeout
settings.summary: The longest one decision call may take before it is given up.
settings.description: The longest the systemone adapter waits for one decision call, from connecting to the whole answer. A call is sent once: a late decision is given up, and its caller decides without it.

settings.title: Largest decision request
settings.summary: The largest decision request sent, in bytes; larger ones are refused.
settings.description: The largest request body the systemone adapter sends for one decision call, in bytes. A larger request is refused before anything is sent. Ollama itself takes at most 64 KiB of text and questions.

settings.title: Most questions in one decision
settings.summary: The most questions one decision call may ask.
settings.description: The most questions the systemone adapter sends in one decision call. A request with more is refused before anything is sent. Ollama itself takes at most 64.

settings.title: Auto's ladder
settings.summary: The models Auto may choose for this person, smallest first.
settings.description: Registry names, separated by commas, smallest first, of the models a chat on Auto may be answered by. A name may carry a size limit, as small-hosted<=100000: that step is passed over when a call's estimated size in tokens is over the limit. A name that is not a usable model in the person's registry is passed over. Empty means Auto is not offered and every chat uses the model picked.

settings.title: Auto's decision model
settings.summary: The model that gives Auto's verdict on each message.
settings.description: The registry name of the decision model that chooses a step of the ladder and an effort for each message on Auto. It must have the decision capability. A held chat's verdict goes to it only when it is local or trusted. Empty means the rules alone decide: the lowest step that may take the call, at the default effort.

settings.title: Auto's step notes
settings.summary: Optional words describing each step to the decision model.
settings.description: Descriptions of steps of the ladder for the decision model, as name=words, separated by semicolons. A step with no note is described by its label and its place on the ladder.

settings.title: New chats start on Auto
settings.summary: A new chat lets the router choose the model for each message.
settings.description: Whether a chat made from now on starts on Auto, where the router chooses the model and the effort for each message from the ladder. It has no effect while the ladder is empty: a chat then uses the model picked. Chats that already exist keep what they are on.

settings.title: Auto's confidence level
settings.summary: A verdict less sure than this moves up one step.
settings.description: The probability, from 0 to 1, under which the step a verdict chose moves one step up the ladder, to the next step that may take the call.

settings.title: Auto's verdict timeout
settings.summary: The longest Auto waits for a verdict before the rules decide.
settings.description: The longest the router waits for the decision model's verdict on one message. With no answer by then, the rules alone decide: the lowest step that may take the call, at the default effort.

settings.title: Message shown to the verdict
settings.summary: How many characters of the newest message the verdict sees.
settings.description: How many characters of the newest message the decision model is shown, with the call's facts. It is never shown the rest of the chat.

settings.title: Auto's default effort
settings.summary: The effort used when the rules alone decide.
settings.description: The effort a message on Auto is sent with when the rules alone decide, as when there is no verdict in time.

settings.title: Auto's highest effort
settings.summary: The most effort Auto ever asks of a model.
settings.description: The most effort the router asks for, whatever the verdict or the default says. A higher effort is lowered to this one.

settings.title: Local machine passed over for
settings.summary: How long Auto passes over local models after one stops answering.
settings.description: How long after a call to a local endpoint, the decision call included, failed as unavailable that Auto passes over local steps and says so on the reply. A held chat with only local steps then fails and says to try again when the machine is back.

settings.title: Monthly cap
settings.summary: The most one person may spend in a month on paid models.
settings.description: The most one person may spend in a calendar month, in US dollars, on models that are not local. A call that could take the month past it is not sent. Zero stops every call that costs anything.

settings.title: Cap warning
settings.summary: How much of the monthly cap is spent before Keystone warns.
settings.description: The share of the monthly cap, in percent, at which Keystone starts to warn that the cap is near.

settings.title: Chat Completions longest retry wait
settings.summary: The longest the Chat Completions adapter waits between attempts.
settings.description: The longest the Chat Completions adapter waits between two attempts, whatever the endpoint asks for.
